summary: Timezone-rollover worker burst triggering tenant 429s and console quota mismatch
description: Issue summary: Multiple customers experienced persistent 429 throttles starting ~2026-03-12T04:00:00Z. Root cause appears tied to an orchestrated worker refresh that executed en masse at tenant-local-midnight after a DST/timezone roll event. Impact: Several dedicated tenants (including SlideStream Media) saw short bursts of hundreds of concurrent warmup/keepalive requests that depleted tenant token windows and caused streaming and bulk endpoints to return 429s. Console quota readouts reported 'tokens remaining' that did not match live throttle behavior (console showed ~30% remaining).
impact: Customer-facing errors (429) for streaming and batch ingestion. SlideStream reported 12-minute service degradation impacting live captioning flows. Estimated affected customers: 4 dedicated tenants in us-east; transient soft throttles observed for ~10 other self-serve tenants. Revenue impact under review; multiple escalation calls occurred.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate timezone/DST rollover by advancing tenant-local clock to midnight while cron workers scheduled without jitter start a refresh cycle.
Trigger orchestrated worker restart across a tenant's ingestion pool (simulate multiple workers starting within <30s window).
Send multiplexed streaming warmup + several small batch embed jobs concurrently from same API key.
Observe token-window depletion and 429 responses from /v1/streams and /v1/embeddings endpoints within 5-15s.
Compare console quota readout to real-time /rate-limit headers on responses to see mismatch.
observed_behavior: Rapid surge of requests from orchestrated workers (peaks measured at ~85k requests/min across the tenant's pool). Rate-limiter consumed tenant burst credits in under 12s. Responses returned HTTP 429 with X-RateLimit details showing window exhausted. Console displayed quota ~30% remaining due to cached snapshot refresh lag and lack of immediate reconciliation with in-memory token counters.
expected_behavior: Tenant-local scheduled jobs should include jitter and stagger to avoid synchronized bursts. Console quota metrics should reflect real-time token counters or flag stale data explicitly. Rate-limiter should handle short synchronized spikes without immediate hard-throttles by smoothing refill or using short grace credits where configured for dedicated tenants.
logs_and_metrics: Edge gateway logs: spike in POST /v1/streams from 10 instances -> 85k r/min at 2026-03-12T04:01:02Z
Rate-limiter metric: tenant_window_tokens_remaining went from 420k -> 0 in 11s
Serving runtime: queue length jumped to 410, per-GPU mem pressure + 18% latency P95 increase
Console metric lag: quota-snapshot.last_refresh 2026-03-12T03:59:00Z while live counters showing exhaustion at 04:01:03Z
Customer logs (SlideStream): repeated 429s with ids: ssm-req-117234, ssm-req-117240
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: misconfigured cron jitter resulted in synchronized warmups at tenant local midnight; confirmed via orchestration logs showing scheduled jobs with identical cron expressions without jitter for several customer clusters.
Observed refill logic uses UTC-midnight reference for credit refill but token-window consumption is calculated in tenant-local time slice for burst accounting -> mismatch during timezone roll events.
Console uses a cached snapshot persisted to Redis every minute; during burst the cache was stale and did not reflect in-memory token drain.
Confirmed correlated Slack thread: #support (thread t-512) with customer screenshots. See link: https://slack.redwood.io/archives/support/p16234
Telemetry shows pattern repeats for tenants with many short-lived ephemeral workers that rotate at local-midnight. Not common but present in ~0.4% of tenants.
Cross-reference: similar customer-impact pattern to SUP-762318 (tail 429s after dedicated pool scale-down warmup) but root cause here is time-sync + cron-jitter absence.
temporary_mitigation: Applied emergency temporary bump of burst credits for affected dedicated tenants in us-east for 60 minutes (operator action: increase_burst_credit tenant_id: ss-004 -> +150k tokens).

Rolled out a per-tenant short-term smoothing policy on rate-limiter to allow 3s smoothing window for synchronized warmups (feature flag: rl_smoothing_short_burst = true) to reduce hard 429s while permanent fix is deployed.
Advised SlideStream to add client-side jitter to their local-midnight refresh cron as immediate mitigation.
Invalidate console quota cache on manual override to force immediate snapshot refresh when anomalies detected (temporary operational runbook step).
planned_fix_and_timeline: Short term (48h): deploy patch to orchestration scheduler templates to inject random jitter into tenant-local scheduled jobs (rollout to dedicated clusters in us-east first).
Medium term (2 weeks): update token refill logic to normalize refill windows across UTC vs tenant-local transitions and add DST-aware reconciliation on boundary events.
Medium term (2 weeks): update console to mark quota snapshots stale if in-memory counters diverge >10% and show 'reconcile' button to force refresh.

Long term (Q2): implement adaptive smoothing in rate-limiter that detects synchronized warmup patterns across workers and applies per-tenant soft-grace credits automatically based on historical behavior.
Customer communication: draft status note to affected customers with incident summary and crediting plan (CS to own messaging).
resolution_notes: Workarounds applied and smoothing flag reduced number of immediate 429 responses to near-zero within 6 minutes of mitigation.
Burst credit increase prevented further degradation; monitoring shows normalised request rates and token counters were replenished by 04:14Z.
Patch for scheduler jitter merged to main (PR #4491) and queued for staged deploy to production dedicated clusters starting 2026-03-14.
Follow-up: billing team to evaluate one-time credit for SlideStream covering 12 minutes of service disruption; CS owner: Priya Rao.
